data.title: BNPL Multi-Provider Application Velocity
data.description: Detects identities applying to three or more distinct BNPL providers within a 72-hour window, a pattern characteristic of multi-provider stacking operations. Legitimate consumers rarely apply to more than two BNPL providers within a week. Synthetic identity rings exploit the absence of cross-bureau BNPL loan reporting to accumulate $3,000-$15,000 in aggregate exposure across providers while each provider sees only their individual exposure. This rule requires consortium-level data sharing to be effective, as individual providers cannot detect cross-provider application velocity in isolation. At Phase 3 of TP-0040, multi-provider stacking represents the critical positioning step before coordinated bust-out execution.
falsepositives: Consumers comparison shopping across BNPL providers for a single large purchase
Corporate purchasing agents setting up multiple BNPL relationships for business procurement
